A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 7Li abundance in the interstellar gas has been steadily increasing over the past 12 Gyr, but that the present-day value is still significantly lower than the primordial 7Li abundance.

the observed 7Li abundance pattern can be well reproduced with a model that includes the contribution of all stellar sources considered, but only with the superwind scenario for the 7Li production in AGB stars.
, although the production of lithium by AGB stars is not negligible, it cannot be invoked as a unique source to account for the observed high 7Li abundance in young stellar clusters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interplay between the stellar sources of 7Li is a critical ingredient to be taken into account in the study of the Galactic chemical evolution of this element.
the 7Li abundance of the Galaxy can be reproduced with a single stellar model only if the mass-loss rate at the end of AGB is high, and if the 7Li yields from AGB stars are large enough.

the Galactic evolution of lithium can be understood only by taking into account all the stellar sources of lithium, and the uncertainties in the yields of each of them are not the only factor affecting the final results.
